headline_finding: The down-market price gap this idea was built on is real, but the position inside it is already occupied by two purpose-built multi-tenant vendors, and Microsoft has begun bundling the capability into the SKU most SMBs already own.

direct_competitors.name: ShadowLock
direct_competitors.pricing: Per device per month, rate card on request
top_features: True multi-tenant architecture described as multi-tenant from the data model up rather than a retrofitted partner view
top_complaints: No public rate card, so an MSP cannot self-qualify the economics before a sales conversation
No published review corpus or customer count, so maturity is unverifiable

direct_competitors.name: Lavawall
direct_competitors.pricing: Published MSP partner pricing model with volume tiers; bundled platform, month-to-month or annual with two months free
direct_competitors.pricing_model: MSP partner volume tiers, bundled platform
top_features: Curated 1,130-item SaaS catalogue with shadow-AI detection
Bundled with CRM and helpdesk for MSPs, avoiding a separate invoice
Explicitly positioned against enterprise per-user CASB pricing
top_complaints: Discovery is one feature inside a broader platform, so depth is unclear
Bundling means an MSP must adopt the wider platform to get the capability

direct_competitors.name: Nudge Security
direct_competitors.buyer: In-house security team, mid-market and up
direct_competitors.last_updated: 2026-05 (added browser-based discovery for shadow AI agents)
direct_competitors.pricing: $5 per user per month for 150-2,500 users; $750 per month flat below 150 users
direct_competitors.pricing_model: per-user monthly with a flat floor
top_features: SaaS and shadow-AI inventory built from broad SaaS feeds
Browser-based discovery that passively observes AI agent context
Established category presence and comparison content
top_complaints: The $750/month floor makes a 60-seat client uneconomic, roughly $12.50 per seat
Built for an organisation governing itself, not for a partner governing many client tenants

direct_competitors.name: Microsoft Purview
direct_competitors.buyer: The SMB itself, via an existing licence
direct_competitors.pricing: Approximately $22 per user per month equivalent, included in M365 Business Premium as of 2026
top_features: Data governance and AI usage visibility inside the Microsoft tenant
No new vendor, no new invoice, no new security review
Already covered by a licence many SMBs hold
top_complaints: Weak coverage outside the Microsoft estate
Configuration burden that a small IT team may never complete

direct_competitors.name: Cynomi
direct_competitors.pricing: Low five figures per year for a small MSP team licence, scaling with client count
top_features: Generates client-facing security deliverables, the exact artefact shape this idea sells
Established MSP partner relationships and enablement
top_complaints: Priced above a small MSP's tolerance for a single capability
Broad vCISO scope rather than deep AI discovery

direct_competitors.name: Harmonic Security
top_features: Prompt-layer inspection of what employees type into AI tools
Real-time flagging of sensitive prompts and file uploads
top_complaints: Two G2 reviews in total, so there is effectively no independent evidence of outcomes

indirect_competitors.name: MSP-channel security platforms (Barracuda SKOUT, Keeper Security, ThreatLocker, Huntress)
indirect_competitors.approach: Add shadow-AI visibility to an existing MSP-sold security platform rather than selling it standalone
indirect_competitors.why_users_choose_it: The MSP already resells them, already trusts them, and already has a billing and support relationship. All four are publishing shadow-AI or AI-governance content to their MSP base during 2026.

indirect_competitors.name: Enterprise DLP and posture vendors (Cyberhaven, Obsidian, Reco, Nightfall)
indirect_competitors.approach: Deep enterprise data-loss and SaaS posture management
indirect_competitors.why_users_choose_it: Chosen by organisations with a security team and a five-figure budget; they define the ceiling of the category rather than compete for SMB spend.

substitutes.description: An acceptable-use policy document plus employee attestation, produced once by the MSP in a word processor
substitutes.cost: A few hours of MSP time per client
substitutes.switching_cost_to_app: Low in effort but the MSP must believe a tool answers the audit question better than the document does. For many audit questionnaires the document is literally sufficient.

substitutes.description: Doing nothing until an audit, insurance renewal or breach forces the conversation
substitutes.switching_cost_to_app: This is the dominant substitute. Only 18% of organisations have a formal AI security policy, which means 82% are currently choosing it.

substitutes.description: Existing Microsoft licence: turning on Purview features already paid for inside M365 Business Premium
substitutes.cost: $0 marginal on that SKU, plus configuration time
substitutes.switching_cost_to_app: Very high as a barrier. Persuading an MSP to add a paid invoice for something the client's existing licence nominally covers requires proving the gap, client by client.

emerging_threats.name: Microsoft Purview bundling into M365 Business Premium
emerging_threats.notes: The classic way an SMB security category is closed: a good-enough capability arrives inside a subscription the buyer already pays for. Confirmed in the 2026 SMB buyer guide at roughly $22 per user per month equivalent.

emerging_threats.name: Cynomi adding an AI governance module
emerging_threats.notes: Already multi-tenant, already selling per-client deliverable generation to MSPs, and already publishing on how MSPs should govern client AI adoption. Adding a module to existing multi-tenancy and an existing partner base is far easier than building both.

emerging_threats.name: Barracuda, Keeper and ThreatLocker extending existing MSP platforms
emerging_threats.notes: All publishing shadow-AI content to their MSP bases in 2026. Distribution already exists; the feature is the only missing piece.

review_mining_summary.most_common_complaint_across_competitors: Pricing opacity and single-tenant assumptions: the two vendors with published SMB-accessible pricing are Nudge (whose $750/month floor prices out a 60-seat client) and Microsoft (bundled), while the MSP-native vendors publish no rate card at all.
review_mining_summary.strongest_gap_signal: Every MSP-facing comparison article argues the same thing, that per-user enterprise CASB pricing does not fit MSP economics and per-device monthly does. That is a real and repeated buyer complaint, but it is a complaint two competitors have already built their pricing around.

review_sources_used: G2 AI Security Solutions category listing
G2 Harmonic Security product page (4.8 stars from 2 reviews)
Vendor pricing pages and published rate cards (Nudge, Lavawall, Microsoft via SMB buyer guide)
MSP-facing comparison content (Lavawall, ShadowLock, Rhindon Cyber, Torii)
MSP trade press (ChannelE2E, Barracuda, Keeper, Cynomi)
review_mining_note: There is no meaningful independent review corpus for this category. The leading pure-play, Harmonic Security, carries two G2 reviews in total. Per the competitor-mapper B2B lane, pricing-page teardown and comparison content were substituted for review mining. The absence of reviews is itself the finding: no vendor here has demonstrated a repeatable, referenceable buyer.

positioning_gaps.description: Clients under roughly 150 seats sit below Nudge's $750/month floor and far below the $25,000-40,000 enterprise contracts, so a per-device price of a few dollars is genuinely unoccupied by the enterprise vendors.
positioning_gaps.evidence: Nudge $750/month floor under 150 users; Cyberhaven ~$40,000/yr with a $36,444 median contract; Obsidian ~$30,000/yr; Reco ~$25,000/yr. But ShadowLock already prices per device per month for MSPs and Lavawall publishes MSP volume tiers, so the gap is priced by others already. Price gaps are explicitly the least defensible gap type.

positioning_gaps.description: SMBs on non-Microsoft stacks (Google Workspace and mixed environments) are not reached by the Purview bundle and are too small for Nudge.
positioning_gaps.evidence: Purview coverage is weak outside the Microsoft estate per the vendor comparison content; Nudge's floor excludes sub-150-seat clients. This is the narrowest genuinely open segment found, and it is a fraction of a fraction of the MSP client base.

positioning_gaps.description: Security tooling is a trust sale and the founder has SOC-analyst credibility, which most vendors in this space cannot claim personally.
positioning_gaps.evidence: Undermined by the channel's actual gate: published MSP vendor-selection criteria require SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and current penetration-test reports from the vendor company, not credibility from the founder. Personal trust does not substitute for institutional attestation in this channel.

saturation_rationale: Maximum on every B2B factor. Direct competitor count: at least six products sell shadow-AI discovery to this buyer (ShadowLock, Lavawall, Nudge, Purview, Cynomi, Harmonic), above the 7+ threshold once MSP-platform incumbents are included. Incumbent dominance: Microsoft bundles the capability into M365 Business Premium, a SKU with a customer base orders of magnitude beyond the 5,000-customer threshold. Funding: multiple funded startups (Nudge, Cyberhaven, Obsidian, Reco, Harmonic, Cynomi) plus a platform vendor shipping it natively, which the rubric calls out explicitly as the maximum condition. Search and directory saturation: MSP-specific comparison pages already exist from Lavawall, ShadowLock, Rhindon Cyber, Torii, MintMCP and Netwrix. Content saturation: Barracuda, Keeper, Cynomi and ChannelE2E are all publishing to this exact buyer. This is a 15 out of 15, the first maximum recorded in this project.
differentiation_opportunities: Non-Microsoft SMB estates under 150 seats, the one segment neither the Purview bundle nor Nudge's floor reaches. Narrow, and it requires an MSP whose client base skews away from Microsoft, which is uncommon.
Per-device pricing published openly, against a category where ShadowLock and Cynomi both withhold rate cards. A real but easily copied differentiator.
Depth of AI-specific discovery versus Lavawall's breadth-first SaaS catalogue approach. Defensible only until a better-funded competitor decides depth matters.
